explanation: In France, showing the soles of your feet is considered disrespectful because the foot is viewed as a low, unclean part of the body. This gesture can be interpreted as a sign of contempt or dismissal, especially in social or formal settings. It is generally avoided to maintain polite body language.
local_tip: Always keep your feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankles, and never point your soles toward anyone during conversation.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest and most unclean part of the body; pointing soles at someone or touching them with feet is a grave insult.
Showing the soles of your feet (e.g., putting feet up on a coffee table) is generally casual and not offensive, though context matters.
Showing the soles of your feet is highly disrespectful as the foot is considered unclean; it can be seen as an insult or provocation.
